    // The variance: lambda^2 * (Gamma(1 + 2/k) - Gamma(1 + 1/k)^2).
    Variance(self: WeibullDistribution): Number
        => self.Scale.Square
         * (Gamma(1.0 + 2.0 / self.Shape) - Gamma(1.0 + 1.0 / self.Shape).Square);

    // The Weibull density: (k/lambda) * (v/lambda)^(k-1) * exp(-(v/lambda)^k)
    // for v >= 0, zero for negative v. Exact — no special functions needed.
    Pdf(self: WeibullDistribution, value: Number): Number
        => value < 0.0
            ? 0.0
            : (self.Shape / self.Scale)
                * (value / self.Scale).Pow(self.Shape - 1.0)
                * (-(value / self.Scale).Pow(self.Shape)).Exp;

    // The Weibull CDF: 1 - exp(-(v/lambda)^k) for v >= 0, zero for negative v.
    // Exact.
    Cdf(self: WeibullDistribution, value: Number): Number
        => value < 0.0
            ? 0.0
            : 1.0 - (-(value / self.Scale).Pow(self.Shape)).Exp;

    //==
    // # ParetoDistribution
    //
    // Parameterization: MinimumValue (x_m, the scale and the lower bound of the
    // support) and Shape (alpha, the tail index) — the Pareto Type I. Support is
    // x >= MinimumValue. Precondition: MinimumValue > 0 and Shape > 0.
    // https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pareto_distribution

    // The mean: alpha * x_m / (alpha - 1). Precondition: Shape > 1 — the mean is
    // infinite for Shape <= 1, where this expression is not meaningful.
    Mean(self: ParetoDistribution): Number
        => self.Shape * self.MinimumValue / (self.Shape - 1.0);

    // The variance: x_m^2 * alpha / ((alpha-1)^2 * (alpha-2)). Precondition:
    // Shape > 2 — the variance is infinite for Shape <= 2.
    Variance(self: ParetoDistribution): Number
        => self.MinimumValue.Square * self.Shape
         / ((self.Shape - 1.0).Square * (self.Shape - 2.0));

    // The Pareto density: alpha * x_m^alpha / v^(alpha+1) for v >= x_m, zero
    // below the minimum. Exact.
    Pdf(self: ParetoDistribution, value: Number): Number
        => value < self.MinimumValue
            ? 0.0
            : self.Shape * self.MinimumValue.Pow(self.Shape)
                / value.Pow(self.Shape + 1.0);

    // The Pareto CDF: 1 - (x_m / v)^alpha for v >= x_m, zero below the minimum.
    // Exact.
    Cdf(self: ParetoDistribution, value: Number): Number
        => value < self.MinimumValue
            ? 0.0
            : 1.0 - (self.MinimumValue / value).Pow(self.Shape);

    //==
    // # TriangularDistribution
    //
    // Parameterization: lower limit Min (a), mode c, upper limit Max (b), with
    // support the closed interval [a, b]. Precondition: a <= c <= b and a < b.
    // https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Triangular_distribution

    // The mean: (a + c + b) / 3.
    Mean(self: TriangularDistribution): Number
        => (self.Min + self.Mode + self.Max) / 3.0;

    // The variance: (a^2 + b^2 + c^2 - ab - ac - bc) / 18.
    Variance(self: TriangularDistribution): Number
        => (self.Min.Square + self.Max.Square + self.Mode.Square
            - self.Min * self.Max - self.Min * self.Mode - self.Max * self.Mode)
         / 18.0;

    // The triangular density: rising 2(v-a)/((b-a)(c-a)) on [a, c), peaking at
    // 2/(b-a) at the mode, falling 2(b-v)/((b-a)(b-c)) on (c, b], zero outside
    // [a, b]. Exact. The peak case is taken explicitly so that the degenerate
    // ends (c == a or c == b) do not divide by zero at the mode itself.
    Pdf(self: TriangularDistribution, value: Number): Number
        => value < self.Min || value > self.Max
            ? 0.0
            : value == self.Mode
                ? 2.0 / (self.Max - self.Min)
                : value < self.Mode
                    ? 2.0 * (value - self.Min)
                        / ((self.Max - self.Min) * (self.Mode - self.Min))
                    : 2.0 * (self.Max - value)
                        / ((self.Max - self.Min) * (self.Max - self.Mode));

    // The triangular CDF: 0 below a, (v-a)^2/((b-a)(c-a)) on [a, c],
    // 1 - (b-v)^2/((b-a)(b-c)) on (c, b], 1 above b. Exact.
    Cdf(self: TriangularDistribution, value: Number): Number
        => value <= self.Min
            ? 0.0
            : value >= self.Max
                ? 1.0
                : value <= self.Mode
                    ? (value - self.Min).Square
                        / ((self.Max - self.Min) * (self.Mode - self.Min))
                    : 1.0 - (self.Max - value).Square
                        / ((self.Max - self.Min) * (self.Max - self.Mode));

    //==
    // # VonMisesDistribution
    //
    // Parameterization: MeanDirection (mu, an Angle) and Concentration (kappa,
    // the reciprocal-variance analogue; kappa = 0 is uniform on the circle).
    // Pdf/Cdf take the angle in radians as a Number, per the type's doc comment.
    // https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Von_Mises_distribution

    // The mean direction in radians, as stated on the type.
    Mean(self: VonMisesDistribution): Number
        => self.MeanDirection.Radians;

    // The circular variance 1 - I1(kappa)/I0(kappa): 0 as kappa -> infinity
    // (all mass at the mean direction), 1 at kappa = 0 (uniform on the circle,
    // since I1(0) = 0 and I0(0) = 1).
    Variance(self: VonMisesDistribution): Number
        => 1.0 - BesselI1(self.Concentration) / BesselI0(self.Concentration);

    // The von Mises density: exp(kappa * cos(v - mu)) / (2*pi * I0(kappa)),
    // with v the angle in radians. IPeriodic with period 2*pi, so no support
    // guard is needed; at kappa = 0 it is the circular uniform 1/(2*pi).
    Pdf(self: VonMisesDistribution, value: Number): Number
        => (self.Concentration
            * Angle(value - self.MeanDirection.Radians).Cos).Exp
         / (Number.Tau * BesselI0(self.Concentration));

    // The order-j modified Bessel function I_j(x) via the ascending series:
    // (x/2)^j / j! * sum_k (x^2/4)^k / (k! (k+j)!), reusing the fixed-60-term
    // `BesselISeriesSum` kernel with the order-j prefactor spelled through
    // `Gamma(j + 1)`. LOCAL to the von Mises CDF below: full double accuracy
    // only for |x| <= 15 (the series regime of the Bessel bodies); the
    // stable general-purpose route for higher orders is downward recurrence,
    // which this deliberately does not attempt.
    VonMisesBesselI(j: Integer, x: Number): Number
        => (x / 2.0).Pow(j.ToNumber) / Gamma(j.ToNumber + 1.0)
         * BesselISeriesSum(j.ToNumber, x.Square / 4.0, 0, 1.0);
